cases.title: a first result writes each row and link, with an insert entry for each
the same result again changes nothing and gives no change entry
a changed row is an update that holds the old value
a row and a link that the scope no longer returns are deleted, and a deleted link has no old value
the change entries of a scope come as rows written, links written, rows deleted, links deleted, each in key order
a real column and a confidence compare as floats, so 2 and 2.0 are one value
a JSON column compares as a value, whatever the order of its keys
two scopes of one batch give their change entries in the order of the scopes
a row that another scope owns is a scope conflict
a link that another scope owns is a scope conflict
a link that is stored with no scope is a scope conflict
a row key twice in one scope result is refused
a link key twice in one scope result is refused
a refused link stops the whole batch, and the scopes before it write nothing
an integer column refuses a number written with a fraction, even 5.0
a row with a column left out is refused
a row with a key that is no column is refused
a row with null in a column that is not nullable is refused
a boolean column refuses a number
a delete in a scope result is refused
an unlink in a scope result is refused
an operation with two verbs is refused
a result that is no list is refused
an upsert to a table that the consumer does not own is refused
a bad row before a bad link is refused as a bad link, because every link is checked first
a bad link before an upsert to a table that the consumer does not own is refused as not owned, because the parse checks each table first
a real key written as 2 and then as 2.0 is one key, so the second result changes nothing
a real key that another scope wrote as 2 is a scope conflict when written as 2.0
an integer column refuses a number past the safe integers as a bad row
a real key keeps the double that JSON.parse gives, near 2^53 and with a long fraction, so a result without the rows deletes each
a json key written as 2.0 is stored and keyed as 2, so a result without the row deletes it
